chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Muhammad, who said: Ali ibn Bilal wrote to Abu al-Hasan, meaning Ali ibn Muhammad عليه السلام.

A Jew died and left a bequest concerning something for his creditors, which I am able to take. Is it permissible for me to take it and hand it over to your followers, or should I carry it out regarding what the Jew had bequeathed?
So he عليه السلام wrote: "Send it to me and inform me of it, so that I may carry it out in the proper manner, if Allah, the Exalted, wills."

key_terms.أُنْفِذُهُ: I execute or carry it out
key_terms.فِيمَا يَنْبَغِي: in the proper manner, as is appropriate
key_terms.لِدُيَّانِهِ: for his creditors; those to whom debts were owed

ai.seo_question: How should the bequest of a deceased non-Muslim be handled according to Imam Ali al-Hadi عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith concerns a legal question about executing the bequest of a deceased Jew and whether its property may be redirected elsewhere. Imam Ali ibn Muhammad عليه السلام instructs that the matter be referred to him so it may be implemented properly, indicating the importance of rightful disposal of entrusted wealth according to due authority and proper judgment.
